historical_transitions.summary: Deployment baseline: FCS created directly (non-proxy) by deployer 0xDe23082005EF4e6Be6170Adb465d4C4a3a099148 in a successful transaction at 08:21:11 UTC; receipt contractAddress equals the FCS address. Runtime code is 11,451 bytes, keccak256 0x9dacc056e5f2d59b75a9c9ae8a3cd5134abf7bfb675462f50c12ab777603cc62. EIP-1967 implementation, admin and beacon slots read zero at this block and the contract exposes no owner. Sourcify recorded an exact_match verification the same day (2026-08-28T08:38:30Z) for contracts/equity/shares/FCS.sol.

Immutability checkpoint 48 days after deployment, anchored to a successful user transaction sent directly to the FCS contract in this block. Two independent archive RPCs (dRPC and BlastAPI) return the identical runtime keccak256 0x9dacc056e5f2d59b75a9c9ae8a3cd5134abf7bfb675462f50c12ab777603cc62 as at deployment, and the EIP-1967 slots remain zero: no upgrade path exists, was exercised, or was available.

Immutability checkpoint 85 days after deployment, anchored to a successful FCS transfer transaction in this block (receipt status 1). Archive reads on dRPC and BlastAPI again return runtime keccak256 0x9dacc056e5f2d59b75a9c9ae8a3cd5134abf7bfb675462f50c12ab777603cc62, byte-identical to deployment; Pacta's own preflight scan at block 26,470,160 independently returned verdict IMMUTABLE_NO_ADMIN with risk score 0.

evidence_sources.claim_summary: Final pre-launch contracts commit 'Rebrand FPS2 to FCS (Frankencoin Shares)' fixes the FCS name and mechanics in public source two days before deployment: an ERC-4626 wrapper over FPS1 that lowers the veto threshold from 2% to 1% and gates redemption on the wrapper holding more than two thirds of system votes.

Repair commit 'docs: add audited FCS mechanics and migration reference' is the first FCS documentation in the official GitBook source, merged the same day via PR #9. The tree one commit earlier contains zero occurrences of FCS and still presents Frankencoin Pool Shares with a 2% veto as the governance token.

gap_windows.summary: For 21 days the deployed FCS governance wrapper (1% veto threshold, ERC-4626 wrap and redemption, vote-shooting of non-wrapped FPS1 holders) had no documentation at all: the official GitBook source contained zero FCS occurrences and still described FPS with its 2% veto as the governance token, until the 2026-09-18 documentation batch (PR #9) added FCS mechanics and a migration reference. Closed block is the last Ethereum block before the PR #9 merge commit timestamp (2026-09-18T13:01:35Z).

executive_risk_memo: Frankencoin's indexed control surface is Frankencoin Shares (FCS), an ERC-4626 governance wrapper over the Frankencoin Pool Share (FPS1), deployed as a direct, non-proxy contract at Ethereum block 25,852,506 on 2026-08-28. Across the full observation window to 2026-11-21 (85 days), two independent archive RPCs return an identical runtime keccak256 of 0x9dacc056e5f2d59b75a9c9ae8a3cd5134abf7bfb675462f50c12ab777603cc62 at deployment, at the 2026-10-15 checkpoint (block 26,199,902) and at the 2026-11-21 checkpoint (block 26,460,054); EIP-1967 implementation, admin and beacon slots read zero at every checkpoint, owner() reverts, and Pacta's preflight independently returned IMMUTABLE_NO_ADMIN with risk score 0. There is no upgrade key, no pause authority and no administrative surface to rotate: control-plane risk for this contract is concentrated instead in its governance semantics, because FCS lowers the veto threshold from 2% to 1%, gates redemption on the wrapper holding more than two thirds of system votes, and can destroy the votes of FPS1 holders who stay outside it. Documentation forensics show a 21-day repair lag: FCS was live from 2026-08-28 while the official GitBook documentation still described FPS with its 2% veto and contained no FCS reference at all, until the 2026-09-18 documentation batch closed the gap (MTTR = 21.0 days, gap window blocks 25,852,506 to 26,004,551). The trailing twelve-month repository audit of Frankencoin-ZCHF/Frankencoin records 87 smart-contract commits against 48 other commits by only 3 distinct human contributors; a single engineer authored 65 of the 87 contract commits, a bus factor of 1, which is the dossier's principal residual concern. Mitigating that concentration, the deployed FCS source was public in the repository two days before execution (rebrand commit f929628, 2026-08-26) and Sourcify records an exact match, so no undisclosed code has ever run on this surface. Residual risk is therefore operational and documentary rather than administrative: a narrow maintenance bench, a demonstrated three-week documentation lag behind governance-relevant deployments, and vote mechanics whose binding threshold depends on continued FCS adoption.

assessment.method: Live bytecode + storage heuristic at the pinned block, cross-checked with Pacta's RPC-pinned record for Frankencoin (block 26458556).
limits: riskScore (0-100) is a heuristic of the controller type and of pause / blacklist / upgrade capabilities read at one block; it is not an audit.

The live check reads EIP-1967 slots, owner(), Safe getThreshold() / getOwners() and TimelockController getMinDelay(); custom role systems, bridge or L2 admin paths and off-chain operations are not resolved.
Documentation is compared only for indexed protocols (catalogMatch), at their pinned block.
